staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the crash against this staged vulnerable checkout. The saved runtime artifacts agree on the libdeflate zlib-header read at `zlib_decompress.c:49` and the OpenEXR wrapper at `compression.c:138`; they differ on which DWA sub-buffer call site inside `DwaCompressor_uncompress()` first forwarded the invalid pointer (`internal_dwa_compressor.h:868` in `sanitizer_trace.txt` versus `:956` in `default_crash_trace.txt`), so the fine trace is anchored to the shared unchecked derived-pointer logic fixed by the local `patch.diff`.

classification.classification_note: Both saved crash traces report a 2-byte out-of-bounds read during zlib decompression of a DWA chunk. The exact DWA sub-buffer forwarded into `exr_uncompress_buffer()` varies across the saved builds, but the unchecked pointer derivation and libdeflate sink are the same.

bug_description.original: A heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) occurs during DWA decompression: while parsing compressed DWA blocks in DwaCompressor_uncompress (internal_dwa_compressor.h) via exr_uncompress_buffer and libdeflate_zlib_decompress_ex, a 16-bit unaligned read (get_unaligned_be16/load_u16_unaligned) can read two bytes past the end of the input buffer for malformed compressed data. This can crash the process (DoS) and may lead to information disclosure or further memory corruption when processing crafted EXR files.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable worktree `_work/src`
bug_description.normalized: The reproduced witness is an OpenEXR file whose header `compression` attribute stores value `0x09`, so `decompress_data()` dispatches the packed chunk onto the DWAB decoder path. `DwaCompressor_uncompress()` copies the first ten 64-bit DWA counters out of the attacker-controlled chunk, converts them to native endianness, and checks only that the fixed header plus the four declared compressed segment sizes fit in `iSize`. On the crashing path, OpenEXR then consumes additional version-2 channel-rule bytes from `dataPtr` before deriving the starts of the UNKNOWN, AC, DC, and RLE compressed sub-buffers, but vulnerable code never revalidates those derived pointers against the true end of the packed chunk. As a result, at least one zlib-backed sub-buffer pointer forwarded through `exr_uncompress_buffer()` lands too close to or past the end of the heap-backed packed chunk buffer for libdeflate's first 2-byte zlib-header fetch `get_unaligned_be16(in_next)`, which over-reads past the buffer boundary in the saved crash. The patch adds `dataPtrEnd = inPtr + iSize` and rejects any derived sub-buffer start/end that falls outside that range before any of the DWA decompression calls run.

source.description: First project-side materialization of attacker-controlled DWA chunk metadata on the reproduced path. The decoder copies the first ten 64-bit fields from the packed chunk into `counters`; those fields drive all later size calculations and sub-buffer pointer derivations.
source.value_from: The reproduced command is `/gt/_work/build-asan-internal/bin/exrcheck -c /gt/poc`. The staged PoC hexdump shows the OpenEXR header's `compression` attribute storing the one-byte value `0x09` at file offset `0x24`, matching `EXR_COMPRESSION_DWAB = 9` in `openexr_attr.h`, so the packed image chunk bytes later passed as `inPtr` are attacker-controlled DWAB data.

sink.description: Common sink reached by both saved crashes. Libdeflate consumes the unchecked DWA sub-buffer pointer as a zlib stream and immediately performs a 2-byte unaligned header read from `in_next`.
sink.note: ASan's top frame is the helper `load_u16_unaligned`/`memcpy`, but both saved traces pass through this statement first and report a 2-byte read starting close enough to the end of the heap-backed packed chunk buffer to cross the allocation boundary.

root_cause.description: Root cause. OpenEXR derives the starts of the four compressed DWA sub-buffers from the attacker-controlled sizes and the possibly rule-shifted `dataPtr`, but vulnerable code performs no end-of-input validation on these derived pointers before later zlib decompression calls use them.
root_cause.note: The patch inserts a new `dataPtrEnd = inPtr + iSize` range check immediately after these assignments and rejects any derived start/end outside the packed chunk.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific decompression gate. The PoC's `compression` attribute byte is `0x09`, which maps to `EXR_COMPRESSION_DWAB`, so the packed chunk is admitted onto the DWAB decoder path rather than ZIP/PIZ/B44 handling.

coarse_trace.summary: The reproduced `exrcheck -c` path opens the attacker-controlled EXR file and runs the OpenEXR core checker on it.
The parsed `compression` attribute selects `case EXR_COMPRESSION_DWAB`, so packed image data is handed to `internal_exr_undo_dwab()`.

The DWA decoder reads attacker-controlled size counters, consumes any channel-rule bytes, and derives the UNKNOWN/AC/DC/RLE compressed sub-buffer pointers without revalidating them against the true end of the packed chunk.
One of the unchecked zlib-backed DWA sub-buffer pointers is forwarded into libdeflate as `(in, in_bytes)` for decompression.
Libdeflate's first zlib-header read dereferences two bytes from the forwarded pointer and over-reads past the heap-backed packed chunk buffer.

fine_trace.note: Source. The decoder copies the first fixed-size DWA chunk header from attacker-controlled bytes into `counters`; these 10 fields drive version selection, segment sizes, and later sub-buffer pointer arithmetic.
The copied 64-bit fields are converted from file endianness to native values before any size arithmetic or control decisions use them.

fine_trace.var: version, unknownCompressedSize, acCompressedSize, dcCompressedSize, rleCompressedSize, compressedSize
fine_trace.note: OpenEXR materializes the attacker-controlled DWA version and per-segment compressed sizes, then sums the four segment sizes into `compressedSize` for the only aggregate bounds check that precedes later pointer derivation.

This present check succeeds on the witness, but it only proves that the fixed 80-byte header plus the declared compressed segment lengths fit inside `iSize` before any optional channel-rule bytes are consumed.

Inference from the source and patch: the crashing witness must reach the version-2 continuation, where channel-rule parsing consumes additional attacker-controlled bytes and advances `dataPtr` beyond the fixed header before segment pointers are derived. Without this shift, the earlier `headerSize + compressedSize` check would keep the later segment starts inside the packed chunk.

depends_on.via: iSize < (headerSize + compressedSize) || iSize < unknownCompressedSize || iSize < acCompressedSize || iSize < dcCompressedSize || iSize < rleCompressedSize

fine_trace.note: Channel-rule parsing advances the caller's `dataPtr` by the attacker-declared `ruleSize`, so subsequent compressed sub-buffer starts are computed from a later in-chunk offset than the one protected by the earlier aggregate-size check.

Root-cause step. The starts of the four compressed DWA sub-buffers are derived from the rule-shifted `dataPtr` and attacker-controlled sizes, but vulnerable code performs no check here that any derived start, or `compressedRleBuf + rleCompressedSize`, still lies below `inPtr + iSize`.

res = libdeflate_zlib_decompress_ex (

fine_trace.note: Both saved crashes converge here: one of the unchecked zlib-backed DWA segment pointers derived in step 7 is forwarded as `(in, in_bytes)` to libdeflate. The saved artifacts disagree only on which caller inside `DwaCompressor_uncompress()` supplied it (`compressedUnknownBuf` at line 868 versus `compressedDcBuf` at line 956).

Sink. Libdeflate immediately treats the forwarded pointer as the start of a zlib stream and reads a 16-bit header from `in_next`; the saved ASan traces show that this forwarded pointer is close enough to or past the end of the heap-backed packed chunk buffer that the 2-byte fetch crosses the allocation boundary and triggers the reproduced over-read.

allocation_context.note: Both saved traces report that the over-read lands in the heap allocation created for `decode->packed_buffer`; the exact region size differs by build (104 or 106 bytes in the local traces), but the allocation site is the same.

cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. Both saved traces pass through `libdeflate_zlib_decompress_ex()` and `exr_uncompress_buffer()`. They disagree only on which DWA sub-buffer call site inside `DwaCompressor_uncompress()` first supplied the invalid pointer, so the fine trace is anchored to the shared derived-pointer logic before those alternative calls.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The patch introduces `dataPtrEnd = inPtr + iSize` and rejects any derived `compressedUnknownBuf`, `compressedAcBuf`, `compressedDcBuf`, `compressedRleBuf`, or `compressedRleBuf + rleCompressedSize` outside that range immediately after step 7, blocking every zlib-backed call that previously could forward an out-of-range pointer into libdeflate.

format.name: OpenEXR file with DWAB-compressed chunk whose version-2 DWA channel-rule bytes shift later compressed sub-buffer starts past the packed chunk boundary
format.contract: The witness must parse as an OpenEXR image whose `compression` attribute byte is `0x09` so `decompress_data()` selects `EXR_COMPRESSION_DWAB`. Inside the admitted DWAB chunk, the first ten 64-bit DWA counters must pass the pre-rule aggregate check `headerSize + compressedSize <= iSize`, then a version-2 rule block must advance `dataPtr` before OpenEXR derives `compressedUnknownBuf`, `compressedAcBuf`, `compressedDcBuf`, and `compressedRleBuf`. At least one zlib-backed segment subsequently passed to `exr_uncompress_buffer()` must therefore start too close to or past the end of the heap-backed packed chunk buffer for libdeflate's first 2-byte header read `get_unaligned_be16(in_next)`, producing the reproduced out-of-bounds read. This contract is intentionally branch-agnostic about whether the crashing build first reaches the UNKNOWN-data call at line 868 or the DC-data call at line 956, because the saved runtime artifacts show both variants of the same unchecked-pointer obligation.
